# A loop limited by an int variable, for i := 0; i < n; i++, is rewritten with an
# explicit limit. n shorter than, equal to and (with a negative n) below the slices,
# and a slice whose capacity exceeds its length, behave like the scalar loop; n longer
# than a slice panics.

exec go run ./testmain
cmp stdout testmain/output

cp ops.go ops.go.orig
loopvec -split .
! stdout .
cmpenv stderr stderr.want
cmp ops_simd.go ops_simd.go.want

env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
exec go run ./testmain
cmp stdout testmain/output

-- go.mod --
module example.com/test

go 1.27.1
-- ops.go --
package test

func SaxpyN(n int, a float32, x, y []float32) {
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		y[i] = a*x[i] + y[i]
	}
}
-- ops_simd.go.want --
//go:build goexperiment.simd

package test

import "simd"

func SaxpyN(n int, a float32, x, y []float32) {
	_vcAFloat32s0 := simd.BroadcastFloat32s(a)
	if n > 0 {
		_ = y[n-1]
		_ = x[n-1]
		for _i := 0; _i < n; {
			_v1, _n := simd.LoadFloat32sPart(x[_i:n])
			_v2, _ := simd.LoadFloat32sPart(y[_i:n])
			_v1.MulAdd(_vcAFloat32s0, _v2).StorePart(y[_i:n])
			_i += _n
		}
	}
}
-- stderr.want --
loopvec: rewrote 1 loop(s) in $WORK/ops.go
-- testmain/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/test"
)

func try(f func()) (panicked bool) {
	defer func() { panicked = recover() != nil }()
	f()
	return
}

func main() {
	x := []float32{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}
	y := []float32{10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80}
	test.SaxpyN(5, 2, x, y)
	fmt.Println(y)
	test.SaxpyN(0, 2, x, y)
	fmt.Println(y)
	test.SaxpyN(-3, 2, x, y)
	fmt.Println(y)
	test.SaxpyN(8, 1, x, y)
	fmt.Println(y)
	long := make([]float32, 3, 10)
	fmt.Println(try(func() { test.SaxpyN(5, 2, x, long) }), try(func() { test.SaxpyN(5, 2, x[:3], y) }))
	big := make([]float32, 100)
	bx := make([]float32, 100)
	for i := range bx {
		bx[i] = float32(i)
	}
	test.SaxpyN(77, 3, bx, big)
	fmt.Println(big[0], big[76], big[77])
}
-- testmain/output --

[12 24 36 48 60 60 70 80]
[12 24 36 48 60 60 70 80]
[13 26 39 52 65 66 77 88]
true true
